pages.title: Chippewa Valley Schools Policies
pages.description: Research and source links concerning Chippewa Valley Schools policies.
pages.body: The U.S. Department of Education [is investigating](https://web.archive.org/web/20260914035351/https:/www.ed.gov/about/news/press-release/us-department-of-education-opens-three-new-investigations-michigan-school-districts-alleged-title-ix-violations) the district for potential violations of Title IX by allowing boys to participate on girls’ sports teams and use locker rooms based on self-professed gender identities.

pages.title: Don Kuntz
pages.description: Chippewa Valley Schools Board of Education Treasurer.
pages.body:
## Race-based views

- When asked how he would improve black student achievement, [he said](https://web.archive.org/web/20260510110625/https:/www.michiganedjustice.org/school-board-candidates-2024/kuntz,-don---chippewa-valley), “Engage with the Black Community and listen to their concerns. Don't assume what is being done for all students meets the needs of this community.”

- When asked about recruiting staff “of color,” [he said](https://web.archive.org/web/20260510110625/https:/www.michiganedjustice.org/school-board-candidates-2024/kuntz,-don---chippewa-valley), “Only then can we begin to think about having success in bringing in more people of color to the profession. I understand why people of color have difficulty with the notion of becoming a member of a profession that gets little attention or respect, when they are striving to elevate their communities that are underserved and disrespected themselves.”

[Endorsed by](https://web.archive.org/web/20260510110625/https:/www.michiganedjustice.org/school-board-candidates-2024/kuntz,-don---chippewa-valley) the Macomb County Democratic Committee.

pages.title: Talitha Mahome
pages.description: Chippewa Valley Schools Board of Education Trustee.
pages.body:
Believes that schools [should have](https://web.archive.org/web/20260610024910/https:/www.michiganedjustice.org/school-board-candidates-2024/mahome,-talitha---chippewa-valley-schools) “regular mental health screenings” and should increase mental health professionals in schools.

## Race-based views

- Claims schools [must address](https://web.archive.org/web/20260610024910/https:/www.michiganedjustice.org/school-board-candidates-2024/mahome,-talitha---chippewa-valley-schools) “systemic barriers” for black students.

- Advocates for “offering diversity and inclusion training for staff.”

- When asked about her thoughts on recruiting and retaining staff of color, she said, “we should be prioritizing diversity in recruitment.”

Proudly endorsed by a gun control group.

pages.title: Rochester Community Schools Policies
pages.description: Research and source links concerning Rochester Community Schools policies.
pages.body:
The district promotes an [equity statement](https://web.archive.org/web/20260814182414/https:/www.rochester.k12.mi.us/about-us/strategic-plan) that includes: “We recognize that systemic inequities exist that create educational equity gaps among various identity groups, specifically those who have been marginalized.”

In 2023 the [board adopted](https://web.archive.org/web/20260814182343/https:/www.rochester.k12.mi.us/about-us/board-of-education/resolutions) an LGBT resolution that said:

- “. . . we acknowledge that this Resolution of support for LGBTQ+ inclusivity within RCS is not complete with any one action but depends on a systematic shift in paradigms and by increasing the understanding of sexual and gender diversity, recognizing that this creation requires appropriate communication, professional development, collaboration with our labor partners, and a commitment from the Board, District staff, and students;” and

- “. . . the Rochester Community Schools Board of Education supports and affirms this resolution, and we are committed to this work; that the Superintendent, or acting Superintendent will distribute or inform Principals, teachers, and families of this resolution, and make translations of this Resolution available on the district website.”

pages.title: Julie Alspach
pages.description: Rochester Community Schools Board of Education Treasurer.
pages.body:
Voted in favor of a 2023 [LGBT resolution](https://web.archive.org/web/20260814182343/https:/www.rochester.k12.mi.us/about-us/board-of-education/resolutions) that said:

- “. . . we acknowledge that this Resolution of support for LGBTQ+ inclusivity within RCS is not complete with any one action but depends on a systematic shift in paradigms and by increasing the understanding of sexual and gender diversity, recognizing that this creation requires appropriate communication, professional development, collaboration with our labor partners, and a commitment from the Board, District staff, and students;” and

- “. . . the Rochester Community Schools Board of Education supports and affirms this resolution, and we are committed to this work; that the Superintendent, or acting Superintendent will distribute or inform Principals, teachers, and families of this resolution, and make translations of this Resolution available on the district website.”

pages.title: Jessica Newman
pages.description: Ferndale Public Schools Board of Education Secretary.
pages.body:
Endorsed by Abdul El-Sayed.

Newman is a DSA member and was endorsed by the DSA.

Newman is a [Director of Michigan Education Justice Coalition](https://web.archive.org/web/20260422201404/https:/www.michiganedjustice.org/about). This organization’s mission includes:

- Eliminate suspensions and expulsions as discipline techniques and replace them with restorative justice such as “peer-led practices that bring students together to resolve conflict by asking questions and airing grievances.”

- The coalition wants to “implement a curriculum that recognizes systems of racism, oppression, and trauma in the past and present.”

- “Mandate ongoing professional development for all school staff on confronting and dismantling systemic racism in education and unintentional biases.”

- “Allow [minor] students to be democratically elected to serve on local school boards and the Michigan State Board of Education, with voting rights.”

- “Grant students greater ability to self-govern, whether that’s abolishing dress codes or allowing youth-led decision making for school policies.”

- “Divest from systems that cause our school communities harm, such as school policing. These detrimental systems exacerbate the school-to-prison pipeline and disproportionately affect students of color and students with disabilities.”
